name: Our World in Data chart API

provider.name: Our World in Data (Global Change Data Lab)

summary: Download the data and metadata behind any Our World in Data chart as CSV or JSON by appending a suffix to its URL.
description: Every Grapher chart on ourworldindata.org has a slug; appending .csv returns its data table, .metadata.json returns units, sources and citations, .config.json the chart definition and .zip a bundle. Topics span health, demography, energy, climate, food, poverty, technology and more, as country-year series with ISO3 codes.

rate_limit.summary: Not documented; no rate-limit headers seen. Responses are CDN-cached.

endpoints.summary: Chart data as CSV (Entity, Code, Year, value columns)
Chart and indicator metadata: title, unit, citation, timespan, last update
Latest data point per entity, as JSON

license.name: Varies per indicator; see citation in the metadata

coverage.temporal: Varies by chart, often 1800s or 1950 to present

agent_notes: Find the slug from the chart URL (ourworldindata.org/grapher/<slug>). Unfiltered CSV is the full chart table; csvType=filtered with country=~DEU or country=DEU~FRA and time=2020..latest applies the filters server-side (verified for ~DEU; the ~ form selects by ISO3 code). Column names follow the indicator title unless useColumnShortNames=true. Read .metadata.json for units and the exact citation to attribute.
caveats: There is no catalogue endpoint here: you must already know chart slugs (search the website or the ETL catalogue).

OWID's own text and charts are described by the site as CC BY, but each indicator carries upstream sources and terms; the license text was not found in the metadata files, so check the citation before reuse.
No documented rate limit, so cache downloads.

verification.notes: Exact example executed; csv returned. No key exists.
